faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Are your calculations compliant with DPE 2021?
faq.a1: Yes — the 3CL-DPE 2021 method from the decree of March 31st 2021. Coefficients come from the official annexes, and our Vitest snapshot tests lock against any drift.
faq.q2: Can I customise the reports with my own branding?
faq.a2: Starting from the Pro plan, full white-labelling: logo, colours, legal mentions, signatory, footer. The generated PDF contains no reference to Réno·Calc Pro unless you want one.
faq.q3: What happens if I exceed my monthly quota?
faq.a3: You're notified at 80%, then blocked at 100% with an UpgradeCard. No surprise overage charges. You can upgrade in 2 clicks, the change takes effect immediately.
faq.q4: Does my data stay in France?
faq.a4: Yes — OVH hosting (Roubaix). No client data is shared with third parties, except AI (Anthropic, Ireland/USA depending on endpoint) and only if you enable the photo analysis option.
faq.q5: Can I export my cases when I leave?
faq.a5: Yes, at any time. ZIP export of all generated PDFs + JSON of cases + original photos. No lock-in.
faq.a6: Team and Enterprise plans: token-authenticated REST API, Stripe-compatible webhooks for events (report generated, case delivered, etc.).

faqPage.q1_q: How do I start my first diagnostic?

faqPage.q2_q: Is the free trial really no-commitment?

faqPage.q3_q: Can I trial as a team before subscribing?

faqPage.q4_a: Save 20% by paying once for 12 months. No commitment to renew: you can cancel at any time.
faqPage.q5_a: Yes, from your billing space. Upgrade: immediate proration. Downgrade: applied at the next renewal.
faqPage.q6_q: How does the Enterprise plan work?

faqPage.q9_q: Is my data shared with third parties?

faqPage.q10_q: How do I export or delete my data?

insulationDetector.title: 🔍 Detect hidden insulation
insulationDetector.subtitle: 4 field methods to spot a doubling or undocumented insulation.
insulationDetector.m1S1: Approach a window with a visible reveal.
insulationDetector.m1S2: Measure the thickness between the frame and the finished interior wall.
insulationDetector.m1S3: Compare with the expected wall thickness (stone 50 cm, block 20 cm + 1-2 cm finish).
insulationDetector.m1S4: A difference > 8 cm likely signals interior insulation doubling (EPS, wool + plaster).
insulationDetector.m1SchemaCaption: ⚠ Compare the gap between frame and interior wall face.
insulationDetector.m2S1: Knock the wall with your knuckles at different points.
insulationDetector.m2S2: **Full and muffled** sound = solid wall (stone, full brick, concrete).
insulationDetector.m2S3: **Hollow** sound = plaster doubling + insulation or air gap.
insulationDetector.m2S4: **Dull** sound = loaded doubling (dense fibre, BA13 on rails).
insulationDetector.m2S5: Combine with thickness measurement to confirm.
insulationDetector.m3S1: Conditions: ΔT ≥ 10°C between inside and outside (ideally winter).
insulationDetector.m3S2: Point the camera 1-2 m from the wall, perpendicularly.
insulationDetector.m3S3: Homogeneous cold zones = correct insulation. Localised hot zones = thermal bridges.
insulationDetector.m3S4: Also detects insulation defects (gaps in blown wool, EPS joints).
insulationDetector.m3S5: Pro tool but smartphone + Flir One module ≈ €300.
insulationDetector.m3SchemaCaption: 📸 IR camera — visualises losses invisible to the eye.
insulationDetector.m4S2: Compare with ambient air: a gap > 4°C signals poor insulation.
insulationDetector.m4S3: Measure relative humidity 1 cm from the wall.
insulationDetector.m4S4: RH > 70% near a cold wall = condensation/mould risk.

measureAssistant.title: 📐 Measurement assistance
measureAssistant.wallTip1: Measure length on the skirting (floor) — more accurate than mid-height.
measureAssistant.wallTip2: For height, take 2-3 measurements and retain the average.
measureAssistant.wallTip3: Deduct openings (windows, doors) to get the useful surface.
measureAssistant.facadeTip1: Measure from outside if possible (cadastre + visit).
measureAssistant.facadeTip3: Tip: take a photo with a known reference object (door = 2 m).
measureAssistant.roofTip1: Measure the ground surface (ground floor or cadastre).
measureAssistant.roofTip3: For converted attic, the developed surface is often 1.3 to 1.6× the ground surface.
measureAssistant.windowTip1: ⚠ Measure the opening (structural), not the frame.
measureAssistant.windowTip2: Width × Height in cm then conversion to m².
measureAssistant.windowTip3: Count roof windows separately (different thermal impact).
measureAssistant.floorTip1: Distinguish Carrez living surface (≥ 1.80 m under ceiling) and useful surface.
measureAssistant.floorTip2: Subtract the footprint of interior load-bearing walls.
measureAssistant.floorTip3: For semi-heated rooms (cellar, garage), count them separately.
measureAssistant.ceilingTip1: Measure at several points if cathedral ceiling or exposed beams.
measureAssistant.ceilingTip2: For converted attic, calculate weighted average height.
measureAssistant.ceilingTip3: A height < 2.30 m often signals an old renovation.
measureAssistant.svgWindowWarn: ⚠ Measure the opening (structure), NOT the frame.
measureAssistant.svgCeilingTip: 📌 Measure at several points (sloped attics, suspended ceilings, visible beams).

glossary.pageSubtitle: Definitions of acronyms and domain concepts used in the platform.

dpe.label: French energy performance certificate
dpe.definition: Official French assessment of a home's energy consumption and CO₂ emissions. Classes A (high efficiency) to G (very energy-intensive).

ges.label: Greenhouse Gas emissions class
ges.definition: Greenhouse-gas emission class of a home (CO₂), A (low) to G (high).

cep.label: Primary energy coefficient
cep.definition: Conventional primary energy consumption for heating, hot water and cooling, in kWh per m² per year.

3cl.label: Conventional housing calculation
3cl.definition: Conventional calculation method used for French DPEs (metropolitan France), prescribed by regulation.

mpr.label: French ANAH renovation aid
mpr.definition: Flat-rate aid from the French National Housing Agency (Anah) for energy improvement works. Amounts vary by income and work type.

cee.label: Energy Saving Certificates (French)
cee.definition: Scheme requiring energy providers to fund part of energy-efficiency works. Amount computed by gesture and climate zone.

ecoPtz.label: Zero-interest renovation loan (French)
ecoPtz.definition: Zero-interest loan (up to €50,000) to finance energy improvement works. Combinable with MaPrimeRénov'.

tva55.label: Reduced VAT for renovation works
tva55.definition: Reduced VAT rate (instead of 20%) automatically applied to RGE-certified artisan quotes for energy improvement works.

rge.label: Recognised as Environmental Guarantor
rge.definition: Certification for artisans trained in energy-efficiency works. Mandatory to benefit from MPR/CEE aids.

anah.label: French National Housing Agency
anah.definition: Public body issuing MaPrimeRénov' aids and supporting households in renovating their dwellings.

bbc.label: Low-Consumption Building
bbc.definition: Energy performance label corresponding to very low consumption (≤ 50 kWh primary energy/m²/year in renovation). Common audit target.

dju.label: Heating Degree Days base 18°C
dju.definition: Annual sum of differences between a reference temperature (base 18°C) and outdoor mean. Used to compute heating needs.

sru.label: Window U-value
sru.definition: Global thermal transmittance of a window (glazing + frame), in W/m²·K. Lower = more performant. NF EN ISO 10077-2 standard.

rValue.label: Thermal resistance
rValue.definition: Resistance of a wall to heat transfer, in m²·K/W. Higher = better insulator. Formula: R = thickness / λ.

lambda.label: Thermal conductivity
lambda.definition: Ability of a material to conduct heat, in W/m·K. Lower = better insulator.

psi.label: Thermal bridge linear coefficient
psi.definition: Thermal loss per linear metre of junction (wall/floor, wall/window…), in W/m·K.

shab.label: Habitable Area
shab.definition: Real area of habitable rooms (excluding walls, staircases, ducts). Used for regulatory computation.

srt.label: Reference Thermal Area
srt.definition: Area used for energy consumption computation. Often ≈ SHAB.

ite.label: External Thermal Insulation
ite.definition: Insulator placed on the outside of walls, under cladding or render. Most performant solution to preserve indoor inertia.

iti.label: Internal Thermal Insulation
iti.definition: Insulator placed on the inside of walls, under a counter-partition or directly glued. Less performant than ITE but more budget-accessible.

vmc.label: Controlled Mechanical Ventilation
vmc.definition: Stale-air extraction system ensuring air renewal. Single-flow (extract only) or double-flow (with heat recovery).

vir.label: Enhanced-insulation glazing
vir.definition: Glazing with low-emissivity metal coating reducing heat losses. Essential for Uw ≤ 1.3 W/m²·K.
